MENTOR: Here's Mentor Practice 2 at 0 s. At this size I can't make out where the three layers sit, so I won't describe it.

The idea: when a layer has a parent, it takes on the parent's position, scale and rotation, and it keeps its own animation on top of that. A null is an invisible layer you add just to be that parent. You put it where the group should turn or scale from, parent Tile, Caption and Stamp to it, and then animate only the null. This comp already does it: Hatch follows Hatch Rig. Two things to know. Children get position, scale and rotation from the parent, but not its opacity or effects. And a null never shows up in the render, so it can't add anything visible to the group.

Add a null with Layer > New > Null Object. Then tell me where the group should turn or scale from: a corner, the middle of an edge, or the middle of the group? If it will only slide, you can say so.

MENTOR: That's how Mentor Practice 2 looks at 0 s. The aim is to get Tile, Caption and Stamp moving as one while each keeps its own animation. You do that by giving them a parent: a layer that passes its position, scale and rotation down to them. Hatch already works this way, since it follows Hatch Rig. Children take their parent's position, scale and rotation, but not its opacity or effects. A null is the best parent for this because it never shows up in the render, so it can't add anything of its own to the group's look.

To start, add a null (Layer > New > Null Object). Then decide: where should Tile, Caption and Stamp turn or scale from? That could be a corner, the middle of an edge, or the middle of the group. If the group will only slide, say so, because then it doesn't matter.
